definition: A technique that combines multiple sets of model weights (such as checkpoints from different training stages or different fine-tuning runs) by averaging them into a single model.
details: Weight averaging techniques, such as Stochastic Weight Averaging, can improve generalization or combine capabilities from multiple related model checkpoints without additional gradient-based training.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. In plain words: A technique that combines multiple sets of model weights (such as checkpoints from different training stages or different fine-tuning runs) by averaging them into a single model. Here is how it actually plays out: Weight averaging techniques, such as Stochastic Weight Averaging, can improve generalization or combine capabilities from multiple related model checkpoints without additional gradient-based training. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Model Weight Averaging.
